sentences.text: Today we head into the tightest water you’ll run: narrow channels.
Think of the dredged ship channel into Tampa Bay, or the cut at Port Everglades.
Rule nine is the rule for these places, and it starts simply.
A vessel following a narrow channel keeps as near to the outer edge on her starboard side as is safe and practicable.
In other words, stay to the right, just like on the road.
So when two boats meet in a channel, each holds her own right side, and they pass port to port.
Now look at the diagram, and find the small boat off to the side.
Here’s the part that matters most to you.
A vessel of less than twenty meters, or any sailing vessel, shall not impede a vessel that can safely navigate only within the channel.
Your charter boat is well under twenty meters.
That ship coming down the channel can’t go anywhere else.
So you give her room, and you do it early.
